primitives.name: Comprehensive Metric Suite
primitives.verbatim_quote: Vision The standard metrics-and-visualization toolbox for **regression** uncertainty: given predictions + predicted stds + ground truth, `get_all_metrics()` returns the full battery — NLL, CRPS, calibration error, sharpness, interval coverage — plus plots, plus **isotonic-regression recalibration** (Kuleshov et al.) that remaps predicted CDFs to be average-calibrated.
primitives.assumptions: Predictions are independent and identically distributed; ground truth is noise-free; recalibration assumes sufficient holdout data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Small sample sizes lead to unstable recalibration maps; non-smooth underlying distributions cause overfitting.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's calibration row structure, where each signal has a standardized evaluation.

primitives.name: Isotonic Reciprocal Distribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: GSE lens This is the **regression half of the calibration-on-wire metric standard**, pairing with verified_calibration's classification half: - Every regression signal's calibration row (player yards, totals, spreads-as-numbers) gets `get_all_metrics()` on the 2025 held-out slice: calibration error + sharpness + NLL + CRPS.
primitives.assumptions: Monotonic relationship between predicted CDF and true CDF; continuous score variable; large enough calibration set.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Discrete output distributions produce step-function artifacts in the reciprocal CDF.

primitives.name: Sharpness Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Sharpness matters — a calibrated-but-vacuous interval ("total will be between 0 and 100") is useless, and this toolbox is one of the few that measures both.
primitives.assumptions: Prediction intervals are well-specified; smaller interval width indicates higher sharpness.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overconfident models produce narrow intervals that frequently fail to contain the truth.

layer2.mapping: Complements calibration error in GSI's joint metric framework.
layer2.telemetry: Average interval width on holdout data

primitives.verbatim_quote: - Its isotonic recalibration is the candidate method for NGBoost output distributions — but gated by the idr-calibration warning: check PIT uniformity *after* recalibration on the 2026 W1-4 live-check; if the PIT shows the Thomae-function artifact pattern, fall back to conformal intervals instead of trusting the remapped CDF.
primitives.assumptions: Recalibrated CDF is correct; uniformity implies perfect calibration after transformation.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge in probabilistic regression is simultaneously optimizing calibration (E[Y|σ]=Y) and sharpness (Var[Y|σ]). Uncertainty Toolbox addresses this duality via the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS), which combines both: CRPS = ∫(F(x)-H(y-x))²dx, where F is the predictive CDF and H the Heaviside step function. Isotonic recalibration transforms the raw CDF F into a post-calibrated G, preserving relative ordering while enforcing E[G(Y)|σ]=σ. However, this method can introduce the 'Thomae-function' artifact—discrete jumps leading to overconfident tails. To mitigate this, we implement a walk-forward strategy: re-estimate the monotone map on fresh holdout data each season, reducing the risk of distributional shift. Empirically, we monitor the Probability Integral Transform (PIT) uniformity; deviations indicate either poor calibration or IDR-induced discreteness. In GSE, this translates to verifying that player projection intervals are both reliable (calibrated) and informative (sharp), with fallback to conformal methods when artifacts emerge.
